---
title: "Examples from the help file"
subtitle: "The examples in help sgmediation2, run in full"
---
<<dd_version: 2>>

The examples at the end of `help sgmediation2`, run in order: the basic
test, then control variables, survey weights, cluster-robust standard
errors, and bootstrapped confidence intervals. The
[overview](index.html) page explains what each part of the output is.

```{.stata-run}
<<dd_do>>
use "https://tdmize.github.io/data/data/cda_ah4", clear
drop if missing(health, edyrs, income, race, woman, age)
sgmediation2 health, iv(edyrs) mv(income)
<</dd_do>>
```

Add control variables:

```{.stata-run}
<<dd_do>>
sgmediation2 health, iv(edyrs) mv(income) cv(i.race i.woman age)
<</dd_do>>
```

Add survey weights already set with `svyset`:

```{.stata-run}
<<dd_do>>
sgmediation2 health, iv(edyrs) mv(income) cv(i.race i.woman age) prefix(svy:)
<</dd_do>>
```

Obtain cluster-robust variance estimates for clustering on `occcat`:

```{.stata-run}
<<dd_do>>
sgmediation2 health, iv(edyrs) mv(income) cv(i.race i.woman age) vce(cluster occcat)
<</dd_do>>
```

Use bootstrapping to obtain standard errors and confidence intervals. 1,000
replications are recommended for serious use; 100 are used here for
illustration.

```{.stata-run}
<<dd_do>>
bootstrap r(ind_eff) r(dir_eff) r(tot_eff), reps(100) seed(2026): ///
    sgmediation2 health, iv(edyrs) mv(income) cv(i.race i.woman age)
<</dd_do>>
```

Obtain bias-corrected and percentile confidence intervals based on the
bootstrapped samples:

```{.stata-run}
<<dd_do>>
estat bootstrap, bc percentile
<</dd_do>>
```
